name: Frank Quattrone

summary.text: Frank Quattrone headed the technology investment banking group at Credit Suisse First Boston during the late-1990s IPO boom. CSFB settled SEC and NASD charges over IPO allocation practices for $100 million in January 2002 without admitting or denying wrongdoing. Quattrone himself was tried for obstruction of justice over an email urging staff to 'clean up' files during a federal investigation; his first trial ended in a hung jury in 2003, he was convicted in May 2004, and the Second Circuit overturned the conviction in March 2006. The same year the SEC overturned a lifetime industry ban against him and the NASD withdrew its charges.

sources.title: Former CSFB star charged by US regulators

facts.claim: The SEC's IPO-allocation matter against Credit Suisse First Boston was resolved on January 22, 2002 with a $100 million payment, an injunction against future violations and new procedures, with no admission or denial of wrongdoing; this was a settlement by the firm, not by Quattrone.

sources.title: Former CSFB star charged by US regulators

facts.claim: Quattrone's first obstruction-of-justice trial ended in a hung jury in 2003; he was convicted on federal obstruction charges in May 2004.
The Second Circuit overturned Quattrone's obstruction conviction in March 2006 and ordered a new trial.
facts.quote: The 2nd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals overturned the conviction in March, granting Quattrone a third trial.

facts.claim: In March 2006 the SEC overturned a lifetime ban from the securities industry that had been imposed on Quattrone, and the NASD later withdrew its charges against him for procedural reasons.
The NASD had charged Quattrone with 'spinning' and undermining research analyst objectivity.

openQuestions: Site claim that Quattrone's '2004 obstruction conviction was overturned on appeal': supported (AP via NBC News).

Site claim that his group 'steered IPO shares to favored executives': the NASD charged him with spinning in 2003 and later withdrew the charges; no finding against him personally was returned. The claim should be worded as an allegation.
The outcome of the government's talks on a deferred-prosecution agreement in 2006 was not confirmed here.
